title: Design a Paste Sharing Service
brief: People paste snippets of text, get a short link back, and share it. Most links are read many times after being written once, and a few go viral. Every paste page also shows a sponsored ad, and pastes expire, so something has to find and delete the old ones. How you split those jobs across servers is part of the design.
constraints: Reading a paste should take under 150 ms
About 15,000 reads per second at peak, with roughly 1 write for every 20 reads
Half of the pages show an ad, but the page must still load if the ad lookup is slow or down
Ads come from an external ad network: about 120 ms per call, and a rate limit you buy by the plan
Expired pastes stop being served and are deleted by a background job

scenarios.title: Regular day
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Why is this workload a good fit for caching, and where would you run the ad lookup and the expiry sweep?
scenarios.debrief: The CDN and cache answer most reads, so the servers and database only see misses and the few writes.

scenarios.title: A paste goes viral (3x)
scenarios.description: One link is shared on social media and traffic triples.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: One key receives most of the extra traffic. How do you keep that single key from overloading a node?
scenarios.debrief: A viral paste is a handful of hot keys. The CDN and cache serve them, so tripling traffic mostly needs headroom on the servers.

scenarios.title: Primary store fails
scenarios.description: The main database node is lost.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: What can still be served while the database recovers, and what is lost?
scenarios.debrief: Two read replicas mean losing a node reduces capacity but not service, and the cache covers most reads meanwhile.

scenarios.title: Ad lookups time out
scenarios.description: Whatever runs the ad lookup becomes 20x slower.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: The ad lookup hangs. What does a reader see, and why does or doesn't it matter where the ad code runs?
scenarios.debrief: Ads are in their own service called behind a circuit breaker with a 60 ms timeout, so a 20x slowdown is cut off and the paste still loads.

scenarios.title: Ad network outage
scenarios.description: The external ad network stops answering.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: You do not control the ad network. What does a reader see when it is down, and how do you avoid waiting on it?
scenarios.debrief: The breaker skips the ad when the provider is down, and the paste is served without it.

requirements.text: Reads meet the latency target at peak
At least 98% of requests are served when traffic triples
Reads are served from a cache or CDN in front of storage
A slow ad lookup cannot slow down reading a paste
Pastes still load when the ad network is down
Something issues short links, and never gives two pastes the same one

rubric: Paste bodies and metadata are stored durably; reads are mostly served from cache or CDN.
A strategy for unique short ids is described (counter ranges, random ids with check, or a key service).
Expiry is handled by a TTL or a background cleanup worker.
The primary store has at least a replica so one failure does not take reads down.
The ad lookup and the expiry sweep are placed deliberately: either inside the paste server (simple, shared fate) or apart (isolated, extra hop and cost), with the trade-off stated.
A failing or slow ad lookup is cut off with a timeout or circuit breaker so reads still succeed.
Expiry is handled by a worker or a TTL on the store, not by competing with user requests on the read servers.

capabilities.label: Serve a paste
capabilities.hint: Read a paste, or create one and its short link

capabilities.label: Issue a unique short link
capabilities.hint: Give each new paste a short code that no other paste has. Two creations at the same moment must never get the same code.

capabilities.label: Show an ad
capabilities.hint: Ask the ad network for an ad to show beside half of the pastes. The page works without it.

capabilities.label: Expire old pastes
capabilities.hint: A sweep that finds pastes past their expiry and deletes them, about 600 per second

reference.summary: Serve reads from a CDN and a cache, keep ads and expiry out of the read path, and issue short links from leased counter ranges.
design: User, then a CDN (cache API responses, 90% hit), then a Load Balancer (2 instances), then a Server with 8 replicas running 'Serve a paste' and 'Issue a unique short link'. Circuit breaker on, 60 ms timeout, ID strategy Counter range per server.
The Server reads a Cache (2 replicas, 95% hit) in front of a Database with 2 read replicas and Row locks. The lock is what lets servers lease id ranges safely.
Ads run in a separate Service (2 replicas) with its own Cache (90% hit) in front of a Third-party API set to Ad network.
A Worker (4 replicas, idempotent) runs 'Expire old pastes' against the Database.
tradeoffs: The separate ad service costs about $400 a month and one more hop, but a slow or dead ad network cannot slow paste reads.
Counter ranges need the database to lock, which costs some write throughput. With one write for every 20 reads that is cheap.
